# Motivation

## When physics lives on the interface

:::{.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- Some physics does **not** live in the volume
- It lives on an **interface**: membranes, films, droplets, bubbles
- A surface PDE is the natural model when the layer is **thin** and **active**
- Geometry matters: **tangency, curvature, transport on the interface**
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
![](figures/Ggb_in_soap_bubble_1.jpg){width=100%}
:::
:::

## Why solve on the surface?

:::{.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
- The unknown is **confined to the interface itself**
- We avoid resolving an artificial **thin bulk layer**
- Surface diffusion, advection, and reaction follow the **geometry of the manifold**
- This is the right language for **surfactants, membranes, and interfacial chemistry**
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
![](images/plasma_membrane.jpg){width=100%}

![](images/blue_marble.jpg){width=78% fig-align="center"}
:::
:::
